title: Just Another F*cking Short Film
synopsis: A wry, self-aware short about making films with no budget and too much heart.
description: Just Another F*cking Short Film — a film by Blue Sheep.
standfirst: The first one. Shot fast, cut close, and unembarrassed about being small.
note: The title is the argument. A debut that refuses the ceremony of debuts — no establishing grandeur, no apology for the budget, nothing in the frame that had to be borrowed to look expensive. It existed to answer one question: could the company finish something.

title: Statuette
synopsis: A character study told in stillness — a portrait of grief, ritual, and the objects we hold onto.
description: Statuette — a film by Blue Sheep.
standfirst: Chamber scale. One object, one room, and everything nobody will say out loud.
note: An object stands in for a person’s idea of themselves. Built around what a room does to a conversation when the thing on the table still has no name. Two people, one prop, and a running time short enough that nothing can be explained twice.

title: Runaway Sheep
synopsis: A coming-of-age story about slipping the leash and finding your own direction.
description: Runaway Sheep — a film by Blue Sheep.
standfirst: The house film. Named after the mark on the door and made with the same instinct.
note: Leave, look back, keep walking. Loose in the shoulders and exact in the cut — the film we point at when somebody asks what the company actually sounds like rather than what it says it does.
pull: Loose in the shoulders. Exact in the cut.

title: DBC
synopsis: A visual study built around rhythm, texture, and motion.
description: DBC — a film by Blue Sheep.
standfirst: Commissioned. A brief, a clock, a budget — held to the standard of the shorts.
note: Commercial work is not a lesser register here. Same crew, same insistence that the frame do more than deliver the product. A brief arrives with a clock attached; the only interesting question is what you protect once the clock starts.

title: Red Hand
synopsis: A tense character study about guilt, complicity, and what people choose to carry.
description: Red Hand — A tense character study about guilt, complicity, and what people choose to carry.
standfirst: Guilt as a genre problem. Colour doing structural work, not decoration.
note: Where a scene sits on the spectrum tells you how much the character already knows, and the film gives that away several beats before the dialogue does. Guilt treated as a genre problem rather than a mood — something with rules, escalation, and a shape you can cut to.
pull: The grade is the second script.

title: Until I Come Alive
synopsis: An intimate portrait of someone chasing the one moment that makes them feel real.
description: Until I Come Alive — An intimate portrait of someone chasing the one moment that makes them feel real.
standfirst: The long gestation. A film about waiting, made slowly enough to be honest about it.
note: Held the longest of anything on the slate, and eventually the schedule became the subject. Patience is difficult to shoot; the only way through was to stop trying to make the waiting interesting.

title: Lost Puppets
synopsis: A tender, off-kilter story about the people we latch onto when we're lost ourselves.
description: Lost Puppets — A tender, off-kilter story about the people we latch onto when we're lost ourselves.
standfirst: Marionette logic applied to adults who have just noticed the strings.
note: Who is holding the strings, and what happens in the half second after somebody looks up and works out that somebody is. Everything built around it — the blocking, the rooms, the length of every take — is scaffolding put up to make that land.
pull: That half second is the whole film.

title: Family Ties x Evo Da Saint
synopsis: A live session capturing Evo Da Saint's sound in an intimate, unfiltered setting.
description: Family Ties x Evo Da Saint — a film by Blue Sheep.
standfirst: Collaboration. Made with a musician, on the musician’s terms.
note: Performance and portrait inside the same take. Working to somebody else’s tempo meant giving up the shot list more than once, which turned out to be the point rather than the cost.
pull: It belongs to somebody else as much as to us.
